author: Kathryn Bruch
title: More delays set back Alabama medical cannabis dispensaries - NewsBreak
text:
By Kathryn Bruch ,
37 minutes ago
MOBILE, Ala. ( WKRG ) — More than five years after Alabama lawmakers approved medical cannabis, only one dispensary is now open in the state.
Jerry Carl wins GOP nomination in Alabama’s District 1 Special Congressional race Callie’s Apothecary in Montgomery is currently the only location operating and selling medical cannabis to patients in Alabama. Co-owner Vince Schilleci said patients are traveling from across the state to get there.
“We have patients from all over. From the Huntsville area, from Baldwin County, and the Mobile County area,” Schilleci said. “And so sometimes it’s hard for them to get up weekly to see us.”
Medical Cannabis Commission Director John McMillan said that about 1,500 patients are currently registered, including many people with chronic pain and PTSD.
The commission previously expected medical cannabis to be available in May, but that timeline was pushed back.
New video shows suspect shooting high-powered rifle in deadly Crestview standoff “I think at the time we were making those predictions, which were a little overly optimistic, and I’ll include myself in that,” McMillan said.
McMillan said money and legal challenges have been the main reasons behind the delays.
“Any wise businessman would not spend a lot of money getting these facilities ready to go,” McMillan said.
Now, the timeline for a medical cannabis facility on the Gulf Coast remains uncertain once again.
“One of my major concerns, being a Baldwin County resident, to not know when we going to be able to take care of a lot of patients in this area,” McMillan said.
Powerball jackpot reaches $1 billion as Gulf Coast hopefuls dream big McMillan said he is hopeful more licenses will be issued, and more dispensaries will open by the end of this year or early 2027.
